description: Phase 9: Upgrade the catch-all message handler in telegram.rs to process pending edit sessions — handle text replies for caption edits and timecodes, photo replies for image replacement. This completes the interactive edit flow started by callback handlers in Phase 4.

steps.task: Modify the catch-all message handler endpoint in telegram.rs (currently silently ignores non-command messages). Change it to: (1) Check if the message sender has a pending EditSession in state.edit_sessions (keyed by msg.from.id). (2) If no session: silently ignore (current behavior). (3) If session exists: extract and remove the session from the map, then dispatch based on variant. Import necessary types.

decisions: Remove session from map BEFORE processing (prevents stale sessions if processing fails)
Only check msg.from.id — the user who clicked the edit button must send the reply
learnings: Current catch-all is at lines 64-88 in the dispatcher handler tree
EditSession enum has 3 variants: AwaitingCaption, AwaitingImage, AwaitingTimecode

steps.task: Handle EditSession::AwaitingCaption in the catch-all handler. When the user sends a text message while AwaitingCaption { artist_id, preview_msg_id }: (1) Extract the text from the message. (2) Update `instagram_caption` in the artists DB table: `UPDATE artists SET instagram_caption = ?, updated_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = ?`. (3) Build the updated inline keyboard via build_artist_preview_keyboard (need to load artist to check track existence). (4) Call telegram_notify::edit_message_caption_raw() to update the preview message in-place with the new caption and preserved keyboard. (5) Send a confirmation reply: '✅ Caption updated'. (6) If message has no text, send error: '❌ Please send text for the new caption'.

decisions: Rebuild keyboard after caption edit (buttons should remain)
Confirmation reply lets the user know the caption was updated successfully

steps.task: Handle EditSession::AwaitingImage in the catch-all handler. When the user sends a photo while AwaitingImage { artist_id, preview_msg_id }: (1) Extract the photo from msg.photo() — use the largest resolution (last element in the PhotoSize array). (2) Get the file from Telegram: call bot.get_file(file_id) to get FilePath, then download via `https://api.telegram.org/file/bot{token}/{file_path}`. (3) Upload the downloaded bytes to R2 as the artist's pic_overlay_key: `artists/{id}/overlay/telegram_upload.jpg`. (4) Update DB: `UPDATE artists SET pic_overlay_key = ?, updated_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = ?`. (5) Rebuild keyboard. (6) Call telegram_notify::edit_message_media_raw() to replace the preview photo in-place. (7) Send confirmation: '✅ Image updated'. (8) If message has no photo, send error: '❌ Please send a photo'.

decisions: Use largest PhotoSize (last element) for best quality
Store as pic_overlay_key — this is the highest priority image in the selection chain
Use edit_message_media_raw to replace the photo in the existing message
learnings: teloxide Bot::get_file returns a File with file_path field
storage::upload_file or similar function exists for R2 uploads
knowledge.notes: The download from Telegram and upload to R2 may take a few seconds — consider sending a '⏳ Processing image...' message first

steps.task: Handle EditSession::AwaitingTimecode in the catch-all handler. When the user sends a text message while AwaitingTimecode { artist_id, track_number, preview_msg_id, video_msg_id }: (1) Extract text, parse it with parse_timecode() (from Phase 5). (2) If parse fails, re-insert the session and reply with error: '❌ Invalid timecode. Send M:SS (e.g. 1:30) or seconds (e.g. 90)'. (3) Load artist from DB to get image key and track key. (4) Send '⏳ Regenerating video from {timecode}...' reply. (5) Call video::generate_track_preview_video(state, image_key, track_key, "", 30, start_offset_secs). (6) Upload regenerated video to R2 at the same key (artists/{id}/track{N}_video/preview.mp4), overwriting the old one. (7) Call telegram_notify::edit_message_media_raw() to replace the video message in-place with the new video. (8) Send confirmation: '✅ Video {N} regenerated from {timecode}'.

decisions: Re-insert session on parse failure so user can try again
Overwrite existing video in R2 (same key) to keep things clean
Use edit_message_media_raw with media_type='video' to replace video in-place
learnings: parse_timecode from Phase 5 step 4 parses M:SS or plain seconds
Video generation takes several seconds — send wait message first
knowledge.notes: Video regeneration is CPU-intensive (FFmpeg). Consider running in tokio::spawn_blocking or a dedicated thread. However, the current codebase runs FFmpeg via tokio::process::Command which is already async.

steps.task: Run `cargo check` from source/backend/ to verify Phase 9 compiles. Then run `cargo test` to ensure no regressions. Fix any compilation errors.
